title: In-Place Swap
goal: Swap the first and last elements of a string slice without moving values out.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 2 Morning: Slices and Borrowing

hints: Indexing a slice of non-Copy items produces a reference, not an owned value that can be moved.
Slice methods like .swap() operate on &mut [T] in place without breaking aliasing rules.
explanation: `items.swap(0, len - 1)` exchanges elements in place safely. Trying `let tmp = items[0]` fails with `E0507` because `String` does not implement `Copy` and cannot be moved out of a slice. Indexing twice mutably like `&mut items[0]` fails with `E0499` because indexing borrows the whole slice mutably, blocking a second borrow. Passing `&mut words` provides the required mutable slice borrow (`E0308` on immutable or owned arguments).
